transcript.raw_output:
Let me get this pre-filing conference started. We have a competitor that's applied to register "NEXORA" in classes 9 and 42 — the same classes where we hold an earlier registration. They've also begun marketing products under that mark. The business team wants us to protect our commercial position without creating unnecessary disruption.

Before I approve any enforcement response, I need each of you to report your findings per our standard pre-filing conference requirements. I'll need reports from the responsible trademark reviewer, investigations, brand, and conflicts reviewers.

Let's go through each area systematically. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Elena, before we go further, I need to flag something critical I found while reviewing the historical trademark file. There's an executed 2019 coexistence letter between our company and this competitor. The letter permits the competitor's class 42 software use — but it expressly allows us to challenge their class 9 medical-device use. This document was scanned into an archive folder but was never added to the current enforcement file, which is why we haven't been working from it. This significantly changes our posture: we likely cannot oppose or challenge the class 42 application without breaching the coexistence letter, but we retain clear rights to challenge the class 9 medical-device application.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something from my investigations review. I've confirmed exactly 14 documented instances in our customer-support records where customers confused the competitor's medical-device product with our company's product. This is direct evidence of actual marketplace confusion, which is highly relevant to our class 9 position. However, I haven't attached these records to the draft filing yet — my evidence index is still being finalized, so the documentation isn't ready for submission at this moment.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share something important from my brand review. In a direct call this week, the client instructed me that protecting the NEXORA mark for medical devices — class 9 — is the priority. The client specifically wants to preserve the competitor's permitted software use in class 42 rather than challenge it. This instruction hasn't been entered into the matter-management notes yet, so it's not reflected in our current file. This aligns with what Noah just raised about the 2019 coexistence letter and confirms our enforcement focus should be on class 9 only.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to disclose a critical conflicts issue before we go any further. I ran the competitor's parent company through our firm's conflicts database and confirmed that the parent is an existing client of the firm in an unrelated tax matter. Under our ethical obligations, the firm cannot proceed with any adverse action against the competitor — including filing opposition or enforcement proceedings — until the competitor-matter team obtains the parent company's informed written consent and we establish an ethical screen. I have not yet placed this conflicts clearance requirement into the filing checklist, so I want everyone to be aware that this is an unresolved prerequisite before Elena can approve any response package.
transcript.speaker: A5
